newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Largest stocks drive Moroccan bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Largest stocks drive Moroccan bourse higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market ended the week on Friday higher driven by the market largest capitalisation including Wafabank and ONA Group, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index rose to 430.70 points from 429.43 points a week earlier.

"The market registered significant movements of the largest capitalisation companies...Investors were monitoring closely the market trading as it became more and more liquid compared with the previous week," Sanae Bennouna, analyst at Upline Securities, said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has interests in more than 40 companies, gained 10 dirhams to close at 600 dirhams on the previous week.
ONA Group, one of the blue chips, sold blocks of thousands shares on the over the counter market during the week, she said.
But the group's shares remained stable at 450 dirhams on Friday compared with the previous week. ONA has a market capitalisation of more than 7.7 billion dirhams.

Earlier this week, it ceded 20 percent of its majority stake in its subsidiary Centrale Laitiere to French Danone. Centrale Laitiere is expected to post positive results or more than 70 million dirhams net profit by end 1996, brokers said.
Samir refinery, Morocco's main oil plant and in which the government expects to sell up to 51 percent stake to foreign oil investors, rose to 251 dirhams, up from 247 dirhams last week.
Wafabank, one the main market capitalisations, gained six dirhams to close at 509.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the bourse's largest capitalisation, lost 40 dirhams to close at 700 dirhams.
The bourse volume on Friday was 23.8 million dirhams down from 222 million dirhams last Friday, stockbrokers said.
